description: Prefix Sum is a precomputation technique that stores the cumulative sum of elements up to each index in an array. It allows range sum queries or subarray sum calculations to be answered in O(1) time, rather than recalculating the sum iteratively.
important_details: Preprocessing: Requires an initial O(N) pass to build the prefix sum array.
Querying: The sum of any subarray [L, R] (inclusive) can be found using `prefix[R+1] - prefix[L]`.
Space-Time Tradeoff: Trades O(N) extra space for O(1) query time. Essential for brute-force optimization.
Limitations: Best suited for static arrays. If the original array elements change dynamically, a Fenwick Tree (BIT) or Segment Tree is required instead.
other_relevant_details: Prefix sums are not limited to addition. They can be used with XOR (Prefix XOR) or modular arithmetic. When combined with a Hash Map, they become a powerful tool for counting subarrays that satisfy a specific mathematical condition (e.g., sum equals K, or sum divisible by K) in O(N) time.

variations.description: The standard cumulative sum of a 1D array. Used to quickly answer range sum queries or find equilibrium indices.
important_details: Array Construction: `prefix[i+1] = prefix[i] + arr[i]`.
Range Query [L, R]: `prefix[R+1] - prefix[L]`.
Can be space-optimized to O(1) if only the running sum is needed and past queries don't need to be answered.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N) preprocessing, O(1) per query. Space Complexity: O(N).

variations.description: Extending prefix sums to 2D matrices to calculate the sum of any rectangular submatrix in O(1) time.
important_details: Construction Formula: `prefix[i][j] = grid[i-1][j-1] + prefix[i-1][j] + prefix[i][j-1] - prefix[i-1][j-1]`.
Query Formula (Sum of rectangle from (r1, c1) to (r2, c2)): `D - B - C + A` (using inclusion-exclusion principle).
Handle boundaries carefully by making the prefix array size (M+1) x (N+1) to avoid index out-of-bounds checks.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(M*N) preprocessing, O(1) per query. Space: O(M*N). Can be optimized to O(N) space if computing row-by-row.

variations.description: Using the XOR operation instead of addition for cumulative properties. Exploits the fact that `A ^ A = 0` and `A ^ 0 = A`.
important_details: Construction: `xor[i+1] = xor[i] ^ arr[i]`.
Range Query [L, R]: `xor[R+1] ^ xor[L]`.
If the XOR of subarray [L, R] is 0, it means the prefix XOR at L-1 is equal to the prefix XOR at R.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N) preprocessing, O(1) per query. Very useful for problems asking to partition an array into two parts with equal XOR.

variations.description: The inverse of prefix sum. Used to apply multiple range updates (e.g., add X to all elements from L to R) in O(1) time, and then compute the final array at the end.
important_details: Update Rule: To add `val` to range [L, R], do `diff[L] += val` and `diff[R+1] -= val`.
Final Array: Constructed by taking the prefix sum of the difference array.
Highly efficient when there are many range updates and few queries, or when only the final state is needed.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(1) per update, O(N) to build final array. Space: O(N). Often used in Car Pooling or Meeting Room overlap checks.

variations.description: Combining prefix sums with a Hash Map to find or count subarrays that sum to a specific target (or satisfy a modulo condition) in O(N) time.
important_details: Map stores: `prefix_sum -> frequency` or `prefix_sum -> first_occurrence_index`.
Logic: If current prefix sum is `S`, and we want a subarray summing to `K`, we check if `S - K` exists in the map.
Handles negative numbers, which makes standard sliding window unusable.
Initialize map with `(0, 1)` to handle subarrays starting from index 0.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N). Space: O(N). The technique easily extends to 2D matrices by fixing the left and right columns and running 1D prefix sum on the rows between them.
